clay_lined_storage_pits.observation: Pits dug below the frost line and smeared with clay keep grain and nuts dry and safe from mice through the winter.

framed_construction.social_consequence: Long timber houses shelter several families and their stores under one roof; the village settles for good around them.

dry_stone_walls.observation: Field stones fitted without mortar make pens that hold the flock and terraces that hold the soil on the slope.

lined_well_shafts.observation: Wattle and split timber hold back the sides of the well, so it no longer caves in or silts up after every rain.

flood_house_mounds.observation: Houses built on mounds of packed earth stand dry when the river spreads over the fields.

stone_wall_footings.observation: A course of fieldstone under the mud wall stops the damp creeping up and the base melting away in the rains.

flat_clay_roofs.observation: Beams laid with reeds and a thick coat of packed clay make a roof that sheds the rain and can be walked on and slept on in summer.

mould_made_mudbricks.observation: Wet mud pressed into a wooden frame and turned out to dry gives bricks all of one size, so walls rise true course by course.
mould_made_mudbricks.social_consequence: Houses can be laid out in straight, repeatable rooms; a family can build a larger home in one dry season.

lime_plastered_floors.observation: Floors and walls skimmed with burnt lime dry hard and white, easy to sweep and hard for vermin to burrow into.

megalith_raising.observation: The great stone is levered onto rollers, dragged up an earth ramp and tipped into its socket as hundreds haul on the ropes.
megalith_raising.social_consequence: Great stones raised by whole districts mark the dead and the seasons; the work binds villages and elevates those who direct it.

central_hall_houses.observation: A long central hall with a row of smaller rooms down each side gives the family a hearth room, sleeping rooms and storerooms.
central_hall_houses.social_consequence: Extended families live under one roof around a central hall with its own stores; households grow larger, and some grow richer than others.

river_supply_channels.observation: A channel dug from the river bank brings water to the edge of the settlement and the gardens along its way.

flood_levees.observation: Banks of earth thrown up along the river and mended every dry season keep the flood off the fields and houses.
flood_levees.social_consequence: Whole villages turn out each year to raise and mend the dykes; the floodplain becomes safe to farm, and its keepers become powerful.

shrine_terraces.observation: The shrine is rebuilt again and again on the packed ruins of the old one, until it stands on a brick terrace above the town.
shrine_terraces.social_consequence: A raised shrine can be seen from every field; its builders and keepers gain authority over the town around it.

courtyard_storerooms.observation: Rooms with sealed doors open onto a shared court, so the stores of many households can be counted, watched and kept dry.

niched_brick_facades.observation: Walls stepped in and out with buttresses and niches stand taller and stronger, and throw bands of shadow across the brick.
niched_brick_facades.social_consequence: Buttressed brick walls rise higher and last longer; the grand façades of shrine and house announce who commands labor.

stone_lined_drains.observation: A stone-lined channel down the middle of the lane carries rain and slops away instead of leaving them to stand.

wedge_and_fire_quarrying.observation: Wooden wedges driven into cut slots and soaked, or fire and cold water on the face, split blocks from the bedrock.

courtyard_houses.observation: Rooms built around an open court give light, air and a private yard for cooking, work and children.

corbelled_vaults.observation: Each course of stone laid a little further in than the one below closes a passage or chamber without any timber.

diversion_dams.observation: A bank of rubble across the stream turns its water into a basin that holds through the dry months.

town_enclosure_walls.observation: A thick mudbrick wall with gates and towers rings the whole town, and the townsfolk mend it every year.
town_enclosure_walls.social_consequence: The town is now a place inside a wall; those inside and those outside become different kinds of people.

herringbone_plano_convex_brick.observation: Loaf-shaped bricks laid on edge in slanting courses, each row leaning the other way, build fast and hold well.

kiln_fired_bricks.observation: Bricks fired in the kiln like pots stand in water and weather where sun-dried bricks slump and melt.
kiln_fired_bricks.social_consequence: Fired brick stands through flood and rain where mudbrick melts, but the kilns hunger for fuel and the woods thin.

gypsum_mortar.observation: Gypsum burned at a low heat and mixed with water sets quickly between blocks and bricks.

dressed_stone_masonry.observation: Blocks squared with copper chisels and stone pounders fit face to face, and walls of stone replace walls of earth.
dressed_stone_masonry.social_consequence: Stone building becomes the mark of kings and gods; masons become a respected and closely controlled trade.

stepped_stone_tombs.observation: Blocks dragged on sledges over wetted tracks and up long ramps rise in great steps over the royal burial.
stepped_stone_tombs.social_consequence: A ruler's tomb rises in stone steps; the state that can build it can also count, feed and command tens of thousands.

wedge_brick_well_lining.observation: Bricks shaped like wedges ring the well shaft in perfect circles, so it can go deep and stay clean for generations.

wadi_dams.observation: A dam of rubble faced with stone blocks across the dry valley catches the flash floods and shields the town below.

upper_storeys.observation: Timber joists set into thick walls carry a second floor, so a house can grow upward on the same plot.

bitumen_bedded_brick.observation: Fired bricks laid in hot bitumen make floors and channels that hold water without a drop leaking through.

standard_brick_proportions.observation: Every brick is moulded twice as long as it is wide and twice as wide as it is thick, so walls bond neatly in any direction.

ventilated_granaries.observation: Grain stored on a raised brick platform with air channels running beneath it stays dry and cool and does not sprout.

pitched_brick_vaults.observation: Bricks leaned against an end wall in slanting rings build a barrel vault without any timber frame to hold them up.

shaduf_water_lift.observation: A pole with a bucket at one end and a clay weight at the other lets one man lift water from the channel all day.

reed_mat_brick_layers.observation: Layers of reed matting and reed cables laid every few courses bind a great brick mass and let it dry without cracking.

stepped_temple_towers.observation: A solid mountain of brick rises in stages to the god's house at the top, faced in fired brick set in bitumen.
stepped_temple_towers.social_consequence: The temple tower dominates the city and the plain; the gods and their servants are seen to hold the highest place.

brick_mass_drain_shafts.observation: Weep-holes and shafts left through the brick mass drain the rain from its heart before it can soften the core.

clay_pipe_socket_jointing.social_consequence: Clean water runs in closed pipes to the palace and the great houses; who is connected, and who is not, becomes a mark of rank.

light_wells.observation: An open shaft through the middle of the house lets light and air down to the rooms below.

ashlar_masonry.observation: Blocks dressed so exactly that they fit without mortar make faces smooth enough that a blade cannot slip between them.

cistern_flushed_drains.observation: Rain caught on the palace roofs is stored and let down in a rush to flush the drains and the latrines.

timber_laced_walls.observation: Timber beams laid through the rubble walls at intervals let them flex when the ground shakes, instead of falling.

colonnaded_porticoes.observation: A row of timber columns on stone bases carries a shady roof along the court, where people meet, wait and trade.
